title: Why Minds Break
subtitle: An Evolutionary and Developmental Programme for Psychopathology
author: Ian Pitchford
description: Why Minds Break by Ian Pitchford: how psychiatry might move from useful descriptions to tested explanations, with a summary of each chapter.
kicker: Book · Ian Pitchford · Kindle, paperback and hardback

cover.alt: Cover of Why Minds Break: the title in heavy black and red capitals on a bone-white ground, above Santiago Ramón y Cajal's coloured drawing of crossing red, blue and green nerve fibres

summary: A psychiatric diagnosis can name a serious difficulty without explaining why it occurs.

*Why Minds Break* asks how psychiatry might move from useful descriptions to real explanations without losing what the descriptions already do well. Drawing on evolutionary biology, developmental science, genetics and predictive theories of the brain, Ian Pitchford argues for two linked classifications rather than one: a clinical description that helps people recognise a difficulty and plan care, and a separate, testable account of the mechanisms that produce it.

Chapters on classification, development, emotion, autism, psychosis, mood, fear, stress and psychopathy show where current explanations succeed, where they overreach, and what investigations could settle the difference. Every claim is tied to its evidence, and the book invites readers to challenge it.

bio: Ian Pitchford studied biomedical science at the University of Sheffield, where he completed a PhD on evolutionary developmental psychopathology in 2001. In 1994 he founded [InterPsych](/interpsych/), one of the first international online networks for mental health professionals, and he was founding editor of the journal *Evolutionary Psychology*. He later worked in research strategy at the University of Huddersfield. His [2001 thesis](/thesis/), from which this book grew, is freely available.
